title: Oat & Slate — Field Layer Catalog
description: A stripped-back product card anchored by stone-surface photography and left-ranged rugged sans type; built for outdoor apparel brands that let terrain and textile do the storytelling, with specs tucked honestly at the corner rather than dressed up as marketing.
philosophy: This template trusts material restraint over compositional complexity. It refuses decorative flourish, gradient overlays, and anything that competes with the tactile truth of the garment photograph. It exists for the brand that has earned credibility through craft — a Filson or Patagonia register — where the audience is a wholesale buyer or a brand-aligned consumer who reads three honest specs as a signal of confidence, not laziness. The room is a buyer meeting or a brand-story slide in a trade deck, not a consumer-facing social ad.
goodFor: Single-SKU apparel feature slides in wholesale pitch decks
Wool or technical fabric close-up reveals with minimal copy
Heritage outdoor-brand catalog pages inside investor or trade decks
Brand-story slides built around a craftsmanship or provenance narrative
avoidFor: Chart-heavy quarterly sales reviews needing multiple data zones
Multi-product comparison grids with dense tabular specs
Slides requiring body copy across more than one text column
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like the opening spread of a trade catalog set on a buyer's table — still, authoritative, and materially honest. Stone or woven-textile photography dominates the right field with zero overlay interference, letting raw terrain and fabric texture carry all visual weight. The title anchors low-left rather than centered, giving the composition an asymmetric, grounded confidence. Avoid anything that signals styling effort: no vignettes, no atmospheric gradients, no ornamental layer elements.
examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; title block occupies cols 1–5, left-ranged with an 8% outer left margin and no right overhang. A full-bleed stone-surface or fabric photograph bleeds from col 6 to the right edge, supplying all visual mass without any text overlay. A single hairline rule below the title is the only structural ornament; deck label or brand mark sits pinned to the bottom-left footer baseline. No page number on the cover.

examples.promptCore: The slide feels like a page torn from a serious wholesale catalog — undecorated, confident in material rather than composition. Hard-split asymmetric layout: photography commands the right field while a lean column of copy breathes on the left, creating deliberate tension without drama. Terrain-honest mood — stone, fleece, and wax-cotton textures speak for themselves against a muted warm neutral ground. Avoid softening overlays on the photograph, decorative borders, icon embellishments, or anything that aestheticizes the spec block.

    <path d="M640 770 L1920 430 L1920 460 L640 800 Z" fill="#a3b59a" opacity="0.08"/>

    <!-- pocket topstitch -->

    <!-- rivet -->

  <!-- Catalog / folio number, bottom-right OUTSIDE image area is impossible (image is right),
       so place it bottom-right of overall slide, set against the textile in hairline accent -->
  <g font-family="ui-monospace, monospace" fill="#a3b59a">
    <text x="1870" y="1030" font-size="13" letter-spacing="4" text-anchor="end">FOLIO 04 / 28</text>

    <text x="1870" y="1062" font-size="10" letter-spacing="3" text-anchor="end" fill="#7a8580">OAT & SLATE — AW26</text>
  </g>

  <!-- left column folio echo / page indicator -->
  <g font-family="ui-monospace, monospace" fill="#7a8580">
    <text x="51" y="1030" font-size="11" letter-spacing="3">P. 04</text>

</svg>
examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid; stone-surface or close-crop textile photograph bleeds full-height across the right two-thirds (cols 5–12) with a hard edge cut — no fade or vignette — at the column boundary. Text block occupies cols 1–4 with an 8% left outer margin: a small all-caps category label anchors the top, followed by a large left-ranged product name and a single-line descriptor below it. Three honest spec lines (material, weight, origin) stack flush-left in the lower quarter of the text column, separated by hairline rules rather than spatial padding alone. Catalog or folio number sits bottom-right outside the image area; no header band is used.
